page.title: Kestrel Porch Cam: one night on battery

blocks.heading: Overnight on battery: a raccoon, a low-battery alert, sunrise and a package
text: One night with a Kestrel Porch Cam on battery: a raccoon at night, a low-battery alert before dawn, solar charging at sunrise, and a package in the morning. Use the path chips under the diagram to compare the **Normal morning** with the morning when the home **Wi-Fi is down at delivery**.

Source: the Kestrel Porch Cam overnight-on-battery design (reviewed). Clock minutes are illustrative, chosen around the times the product team gave. Battery figures use the design's estimates: about 1% an hour idle, about 1% per clip, and about 3–4% an hour from morning sun (3% used here). Between the check-ins drawn as steps, the app's battery card shows the latest regular half-hourly check-in (1:00, 6:30 and 8:00 AM); their exact minutes are illustrative too.

Note: at about 1% an hour, 25% at 10:30 PM would reach 20% around 2:30 AM, earlier than the 4 AM alert shown here. Both are kept, so the camera's exact battery level between 10:30 PM and 4:00 AM is left blank.

The camera screen shows illustrative animated clips, not real footage: REC while the camera records, PLAYING when the resident plays a saved clip, and STANDBY otherwise. Live view is out of scope in the design, so nothing is streamed between clips. On the map, the camera's motion sensor watches the porch the whole night; each event is detected first, and recording starts in the next step. Continuous sensing is not continuous recording.
bullets: **The app only knows what the camera last told it.** The camera checks in every 30 minutes with its battery level and whether it's charging; the app shows that reading and when it arrived.
**Why the alert came at night:** the low-battery alert goes out on the *first* check-in at or below 20%, whatever the hour. It's sent once, and not again until the battery is back above 30%.
**Animals don't alert:** clips recognized as an animal are saved to the timeline with no alert (default setting). People and packages do alert.

bullets.text: **Why the package alert was late:** with home Wi-Fi down, the camera keeps recording to its memory card and retries every 2 minutes. The alert can only go out after Wi-Fi returns and the clip uploads.
sub: During a short outage the app still says *Online* with an older update time. It marks the camera offline only after two missed check-ins (60 minutes).

steps.text: 10:30 PM, Thursday. The resident goes to bed. The Porch Cam is on battery at 25% and not charging. Its regular half-hourly check-in sends that through the home Wi-Fi, and the app's battery card reads 25%, last report 10:30 PM.

codeRefs.label: heartbeat route
codeRefs.purpose: Accepts a heartbeat and writes battery/charging to device-shadow

steps.text: 1:04 AM. A raccoon steps onto the porch. The camera's motion sensor, which watches the porch all night, detects it. Nothing is recorded yet: the screen still shows STANDBY. The exact battery level overnight is left blank (see the note above).

battery.detail: Last report 1:00 AM · level not specified

steps.text: 1:04 AM. Triggered by that motion, the camera wakes and records the raccoon crossing the porch: a clip of about 20 seconds, which costs about 1% of battery. The motion sensor keeps watching while it records.
1:05 AM. The camera uploads the clip through the home Wi-Fi. Kestrel recognizes an **animal**, so the clip is saved to the timeline and **no alert** is sent. The phone stays quiet.

steps.text: 4:00 AM, still dark. The routine check-in reports **20%**, the low-battery line. Kestrel marks the camera low on battery and sends one alert, *Porch Cam battery low*, to the phone. It fires now because this is the first check-in at or below 20%, whatever the hour.

steps.text: 6:50 AM. Sunrise. The solar panel starts charging the camera (see the battery panel). The app still shows *On battery, not charging* and 18% from the 6:30 AM check-in, because the camera hasn't reported the change yet.
7:00 AM. The next check-in reports that the camera is charging. The app switches to *Solar charging* with the solar icon. The battery card keeps its low-battery icon, which clears only above 30%.

steps.text: 8:12 AM. A courier walks up to the front door and the camera's motion sensor detects them. Nothing is recorded yet: the screen still shows STANDBY. The app's battery card shows 21% from the 8:00 AM check-in.
8:12 AM. Triggered by that motion, the camera wakes and records the courier dropping a package at the front door, which costs about 1% of battery.
8:12 AM. Seconds later the clip uploads through the home Wi-Fi, and Kestrel recognizes a **package**.

steps.text: 8:13 AM. The resident opens the Kestrel app and plays the package clip. The camera page still shows 21% from the 8:00 AM check-in, solar charging, online; the timeline lists the package and the 1:04 AM animal clip.

steps.text: 8:08 AM. The home Wi-Fi goes down. The app still shows 21% from the 8:00 AM check-in.
8:12 AM. A courier walks up to the front door. The camera's motion sensor detects them, even with the home Wi-Fi down. Nothing is recorded yet: the screen still shows STANDBY.

8:12 AM. Triggered by that motion, the camera records the courier dropping a package to its memory card (about 1% of battery), but it can't reach the home Wi-Fi. Nothing is sent, so **no alert** goes out.

8:20 AM. Still no Wi-Fi. The camera keeps retrying every 2 minutes. The app still looks normal: *Online*, 21%, last report 8:00 AM. It would only mark the camera offline after 60 minutes without check-ins.

pkgclip.banner: Clip on memory card · Wi-Fi down

steps.text: 8:22 AM. Wi-Fi is back. The camera uploads the saved clip, Kestrel recognizes a **package**, and the camera checks in. The app now reads 21%, last report 8:22 AM.
